extraction_scope: worker-6 source-reviewed final mechanism adjudication from XML sections and figures

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Spa31 directly disrupts bacterial membrane integrity in S. aureus and P. aeruginosa, including SEM-observed cell damage, increased PI staining, outer-membrane permeabilization, ATP release, and ROS production.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Mechanism is supported for Spa31 and tested bacterial targets; do not generalize direct membrane mechanism to Spa20/Spa22/Spa14 without separate assays.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: LPS addition reduced Spa31 suppression of P. aeruginosa growth in a dose-dependent manner, supporting interaction with bacterial surface LPS before or during outer-membrane action.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The local source supports an LPS interaction context but does not provide a binding constant.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Spa31 inhibited P. aeruginosa biofilm formation and reduced mature biofilm viability in source Figure 7 assays.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Biofilm effect is a functional antimicrobial phenotype, not a standalone molecular mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Spa31 improved survival in a P. aeruginosa-infected zebrafish model, with 10 µg treatment reported as significant.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Spa31 in zebrafish P. aeruginosa infection model
mechanism_claims.limitations: In vivo protection is source-supported but does not establish pharmacokinetics or clinical efficacy.
